evidence.note: Repeated SetTodoList calls maintain a structured, dependency-ordered list of remaining crates/work — a consolidated view of what's left.

Agent repeatedly runs `cargo test --workspace --no-run`, counts and categorizes compile errors, and tracks quantified deltas ('370 remain, down from ~594', 'only 20 left', 'only 3 left') — genuine progress accounting, but of build errors rather than test pass/fail.
Early attempts to run the full test suite and grep 'test result:' lines, but this never becomes a sustained per-binary pass-count ledger.
After a subagent timed out, agent re-checked progress via error count — some state re-verification, but no systematic regression/thrashing detection across shared-crate edits.

reasoning: The agent periodically runs build/test-compile passes and works down a consolidated, todo-list-backed picture of remaining errors, even quantifying deltas (594→370→20→3), which is solidly the level-5 behavior of roughly tracking remaining work. It never reaches the level-8 bar: there is no per-binary test pass-count ledger, no explicit watching for downstream test regressions when editing shared crates, and no deliberate detection of circular debugging — partly because the visible trajectory ends still in the compilation-fixing phase. The quantified error deltas are a mild strength but stay short of true per-binary pass/fail accounting.
